title: Divisions: choosing the dividend and the divisor
header: Divisions: choosing the dividend and the divisor

text.text:
### Prerequisites

This text presents an application for practicing division. Before using it, we recommend studying the previous texts in this chapter (<htcite0>), which introduce the multiplication tables and other basic ideas you will need here.

### Practice Reading a text is a good start, but truly understanding division takes practice. In this application, you choose the numbers yourself: write a **dividend** from 0 to 9999 and select a **divisor** from 1 to 9, then press **Start**. The **multiplication table** of the divisor appears above the exercise to help you at every step. The exercise uses the **long division algorithm** (), the step-by-step method for dividing numbers by hand. Remember: when one number does not divide another exactly, the amount that is left over is called the **remainder**. The application shows the division and asks for the first quotient digit. Write it in the active box. When the digit is correct, the application shows the product of that step; then write the result of the subtraction in the box that appears. As soon as the subtraction is correct, the application moves to the next quotient digit. If you write a digit that is not correct, the application shows a hint and you can try again. When you finish, you will receive a medal (). Click the right arrow () to start a new calculation with the numbers in the boxes, or click the redo button () to redo the last calculation with the same numbers. The **Division format** buttons let you choose how the division is written: with the **Result below** the bar (as in many schoolbooks) or with the **Result on top** of it (a format that appears in historical mathematical documents).
